wiki_paras: Haley Stevens took 548,345 views, the top read on Wikipedia in this snapshot. The runner-up, Learjet 60, managed 263,003, which leaves a lead of 2.1 times. That is a wide gap for a name that appears nowhere else in the feeds. No news item, trend or cluster in the data mentions Stevens.

The surrounding names offer a partial clue. Abdul El-Sayed sits fourth with 243,340 views, and the data carries an American election: Mastodon expects one tomorrow, and Polymarket's busiest contracts are midterm control of the House and Senate. One of them lists Michigan. The snapshot does not say the pages are connected, so that stays a suspicion.

Two other entries are a different matter. Learjet 60 and the Palm Beach County crash article together took 483,962 views, and Susan Saint James added 252,010 with no explanation anywhere in the feeds. Taken together, the list is a mixed bill: possibly an election, a crash told twice, and one visitor nobody else invited.
letter_paras: This is a one-subject day with a crowded margin. The subject is the American midterms, which fill Polymarket's three busiest contracts and appear in one Mastodon post. Around it sit a Learjet crash that took two Wikipedia slots, an M5.3 quake near Greece, and a Hacker News post about Qwen weights at 2,327 points, the biggest score on that site today.

In the quieter corners, DiscImageStudio, which burns artwork onto CDs, DVDs and Blu-ray discs, drew 113 points on Hacker News. Product Hunt's third-place entry is called /dev/null and has 523 votes. Three of Cloudflare's five busiest domains belong to Google. Wallpaper Engine peaked at 110,549 players on Steam, a lot of people redecorating screens.

A same-hour snapshot removes the usual cheat of comparing feeds from different moments. When Wikipedia, Polymarket and Mastodon agree, they agree at once, not because one fed the other later. When they do not, as with Susan Saint James today, the silence is also a finding. Tomorrow's edition will make the same measurement under different weather.

brief: An American election runs through three feeds: Polymarket's busiest contracts price House and Senate control, with Democrats at 95 percent for the House on $4 million, and Mastodon is already nervous about it. Wikipedia's top name, Haley Stevens, led by 2.1 times, though no feed says why. A Learjet 60 crash took two more of the top five slots.
